description: Valid and invalid 2.2 sources outside the gate-1 corpus with state machines in every 2.2 shape (WP5): a timer and an input at the same instant, self transitions that restart timers, inputs discarded with noEnabledTransition and inactiveOwner, ordered transitions with guards on one member and equal timer expiries, entry and exit actions that suspend on waits and requests with a timer expiring during a suspended entry and input queued during actions, machines in a multiplicity family, a receive guard reading another operation's attribute, timer-only machines, a case that drives a machine, and defer as an ordinary name in every position (package, qualified package, enum literal, field, port, port member, parameter, state, operation, attribute, local, connection, requirement, test) together with states and members named when, to and after, and the 2.2 state diagnostics that name them. In 2.3 defer becomes a contextual word and states gain completion, internal and guarded-timer transitions and deferrals (WP5-G01 to WP5-G03); none of these sources uses them, so their reactions must keep the 2.2 order (WP5-R11). Each parses with the kept 2.2 grammar. Their diagnostics (with related information), normalized ASTs and runs are recorded once from implementation 3.1.0 in recorded-wp5.json and compared by scripts/compatibility-2-2-extended.mjs.

models.name: r1 a timer and an input at the same instant: the elapsed timer is selected first (runs)
r2 a self transition restarts the state timers; exit and entry run each time (runs)
r3 discardInput: no enabled transition (guards false) and inactive owner (no transition in the state) (runs)
r4 ordered transitions with guards on one member and equal timer expiries in declaration order (runs)
r5 entry and exit actions that suspend; a timer expires during a suspended entry; input queued during actions (runs)
r6 machines in a multiplicity family keep separate states, timers and queues (runs)
n1 defer as an ordinary name in every position: package, enum literal, field, port, port member, parameter, state, operation, attribute, local, connection (runs)
n2 defer as a statement start: assignment, call and field place inside entry actions and effects (runs)
n3 states and members named when, to and after (quoted where reserved) (runs)
n4 defer in qualified names, imports, cases, requirements and connections (cases)
i1 diagnostics that name a state or member called defer (invalid)
i2 2.2 state rule messages: guards with effects, duplicate actions, parameters, return, unknown initial (invalid)
i3 two owners of one member: a machine and a schedule entry; an unhandled required member (invalid)
r7 a receive guard reading an attribute written by another operation; default policies on events a state does not handle (runs)
r8 a machine whose states have only timers, with equal expiries and a chain of zero-wait reactions (runs)
r9 a test drives a machine through its actor port and inspects its state attribute (cases)
r10 input for two members queued while the machine is busy: the queue created first is served first, the 2.2 queue walk (runs)
